entities.name: Green bomber worm
entities.fact: Green bomber worms drop glowing green "bombs" from their bodies to distract predators in the deep sea.

entities.name: Pearlside
entities.fact: Pearlsides are small fish with rows of light organs on their undersides that help them blend with the dim light from above.

entities.name: Rockpool prawn
entities.fact: The rockpool prawn is almost transparent, with fine brownish stripes, and is common in shallow rock pools around Europe.

entities.name: Heteropod
entities.fact: Heteropods are swimming sea snails whose glassy transparent bodies are almost invisible in open water.

entities.name: Phyllosoma larva
entities.fact: The phyllosoma larva of spiny and slipper lobsters is flat, leaf-shaped and as clear as glass while it drifts in the plankton.

entities.name: Yellowstone cutthroat trout
entities.fact: Yellowstone cutthroat trout take their name from the red slash under the jaw and are native to the Yellowstone River basin.

entities.name: Westslope cutthroat trout
entities.fact: The westslope cutthroat trout lives on both sides of the northern Rocky Mountains and is the state fish of Montana.

entities.name: Greenback cutthroat trout
entities.fact: The greenback cutthroat trout is the state fish of Colorado and has been the focus of long conservation efforts after it nearly vanished.

entities.name: Rio Grande cutthroat trout
entities.fact: The Rio Grande cutthroat trout is the state fish of New Mexico and lives in cold mountain headwaters.

entities.name: Bonneville cutthroat trout
entities.fact: The Bonneville cutthroat trout is the state fish of Utah and descends from fish of the vast ancient Lake Bonneville.

entities.name: Paiute cutthroat trout
entities.fact: The Paiute cutthroat trout is native to a single small stream system in California's Sierra Nevada.

entities.name: Redband trout
entities.fact: Redband trout are rainbow trout of the dry interior of western North America, adapted to warm and harsh streams.

entities.name: Little Kern golden trout
entities.fact: The Little Kern golden trout is native to a single river basin in California's southern Sierra Nevada.

entities.name: Amago salmon
entities.fact: The amago is a subspecies of masu salmon that lives in the rivers of western Japan and carries red spots along its flanks.

entities.name: Biwa trout
entities.fact: The biwa trout is a subspecies of masu salmon found only in Lake Biwa in Japan, from which it runs up streams to spawn.

entities.name: Ferox trout
entities.fact: Ferox trout are large, long-lived, fish-eating brown trout of deep lakes in Britain and Ireland.

entities.name: Gillaroo
entities.fact: The gillaroo is an Irish lake trout with a thick, muscular stomach for crushing the snails and shrimps it eats.

entities.name: Carpione
entities.fact: The carpione is a rare trout found nowhere in the world except Italy's Lake Garda.

entities.name: White-spotted char
entities.fact: The white-spotted char is a pale-spotted char of Japan, Korea and Russia, known as iwana in Japan.

entities.name: Giant mudskipper
entities.fact: The giant mudskipper is the largest of its kind, about 25 centimetres long, and digs deep mud burrows that hold pockets of air.

entities.name: Striped snakehead
entities.fact: The striped snakehead gulps air and can bury itself in mud to survive the dry season.

entities.name: Moonlight gourami
entities.fact: The moonlight gourami is a silvery fish of Southeast Asia that gulps air at the surface with a labyrinth organ.

entities.name: Snakeskin gourami
entities.fact: The snakeskin gourami, named for its scaly patterning, breathes air with a labyrinth organ and is widely eaten in Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Chocolate gourami
entities.fact: The chocolate gourami is a small brown fish of Southeast Asian swamps that gulps air at the surface.

entities.name: Croaking gourami
entities.fact: Croaking gouramis make croaking sounds with tendons in their pectoral fins and gulp air with a labyrinth organ.

entities.name: Florida gar
entities.fact: The Florida gar is a long-snouted fish that gulps air at the surface with a swim bladder lined with blood vessels.

entities.name: Shortnose gar
entities.fact: The shortnose gar lives in the Mississippi basin and gulps air at the surface to survive in warm, stagnant water.

entities.name: Indo-Pacific tarpon
entities.fact: The Indo-Pacific tarpon gulps air at the surface, which lets it live in low-oxygen mangrove pools and ponds.

entities.name: Clown knifefish
entities.fact: The clown knifefish is a spotted, knife-shaped fish of Southeast Asia that rises to gulp air.

entities.name: Longjaw mudsucker
entities.fact: The longjaw mudsucker is a Pacific coast goby that can breathe air and survive for hours out of water on mudflats.

entities.name: Tompot blenny
entities.fact: The tompot blenny peers from rock crevices with branched tentacles above its eyes and fiercely defends its chosen hole.

entities.name: Shanny
entities.fact: The shanny is a common rock pool fish that can survive out of water for hours by sheltering damp under seaweed.

entities.name: Dahlia anemone
entities.fact: The dahlia anemone sticks gravel and shell fragments to its warty column and is often found in rock pools.

entities.name: Black leather chiton
entities.fact: The black leather chiton has a tough dark girdle covering most of its eight plates and grazes seaweed on Pacific shores.

entities.name: Purple shore crab
entities.fact: The purple shore crab of the Pacific coast has purple spots on its claws and hides under rocks in the intertidal zone.

entities.name: Striped shore crab
entities.fact: The striped shore crab has dark stripes on its square shell and can breathe air as it roams rocks above the waterline.

entities.name: Seven-armed starfish
entities.fact: The seven-armed starfish has seven arms rather than five and hunts other starfish and brittle stars in the north-east Atlantic.

entities.name: Black brittle star
entities.fact: The black brittle star lives in dense beds on north-east Atlantic seabeds, lifting its arms into the current to catch food.

entities.name: Common brittle star
entities.fact: The common brittle star can form carpets of millions of animals on the seabed, each holding its arms up to trap food.

entities.name: Giant basket star
entities.fact: The giant basket star of the Caribbean spreads its finely branched arms like a net at night to trap plankton.

entities.name: Rosy feather star
entities.fact: The rosy feather star is a crinoid of north-east Atlantic coasts that can swim by waving its ten feathery arms.

entities.name: Rock-boring urchin
entities.fact: Rock-boring urchins grind snug hollows into coral rock with their teeth and spines and sit inside them.

entities.name: Collector urchin
entities.fact: The collector urchin covers itself with shell and seaweed fragments, and is used in Hawaii to help control invasive algae.

entities.name: Shingle urchin
entities.fact: The shingle urchin has flat, blunt spines that fit together like roof tiles, helping it hold on in pounding surf.

entities.name: Eccentric sand dollar
entities.fact: The eccentric sand dollar of the Pacific coast stands tilted in the sand with its rear edge up to catch food drifting in the current.

entities.name: Prickly redfish
entities.fact: The prickly redfish is one of the largest sea cucumbers and is covered in spiky red-orange bumps.

entities.name: Giant California sea cucumber
entities.fact: The giant California sea cucumber is a large sea cucumber of the north-east Pacific that is harvested commercially for food.

entities.name: Cotton spinner
entities.fact: When threatened, the cotton spinner shoots out sticky white threads that tangle around an attacker.

entities.name: Banco Chinchorro
entities.fact: Banco Chinchorro is a large Mexican coral atoll off the Yucatan coast and a biosphere reserve littered with shipwrecks.

entities.name: Alacranes Reef
entities.fact: Alacranes Reef, off Mexico's Yucatan coast, is the largest coral reef system in the Gulf of Mexico.

entities.name: Looe Key reef
entities.fact: Looe Key reef in the Florida Keys is named after HMS Looe, a British warship wrecked on it in 1744.

entities.name: Carysfort Reef
entities.fact: Carysfort Reef in the Florida Keys is marked by an iron screw-pile lighthouse built in the 1850s.

entities.name: Elphinstone Reef
entities.fact: Elphinstone Reef is a long Red Sea reef off Egypt, famed for oceanic whitetip sharks and soft coral walls.

entities.name: Daedalus Reef
entities.fact: Daedalus Reef is a remote Red Sea reef in open water, topped by a lighthouse, where hammerhead sharks gather.

entities.name: Abu Nuhas
entities.fact: Abu Nuhas is a Red Sea reef at the mouth of the Gulf of Suez on which several ships have been wrecked.

entities.name: Great Astrolabe Reef
entities.fact: The Great Astrolabe Reef is a large barrier reef surrounding the Fijian island of Kadavu.

entities.name: Rainbow Reef
entities.fact: Rainbow Reef in Fiji's Somosomo Strait is known for the Great White Wall, a drop-off draped in white soft coral.

entities.name: Middleton Reef
entities.fact: Middleton Reef is a remote coral reef in the Tasman Sea, north of Lord Howe Island, with several shipwrecks.

entities.name: Kure Atoll
entities.fact: Kure Atoll, at the northern end of the Hawaiian chain, is the northernmost coral atoll in the world.

entities.name: Fakarava
entities.fact: Fakarava, in French Polynesia's Tuamotu islands, is a UNESCO biosphere reserve famed for its walls of grey reef sharks.

entities.name: Røst Reef
entities.fact: Røst Reef off Norway's Lofoten islands is one of the largest known cold-water coral reefs, built by Lophelia coral.

entities.name: Pulley Ridge
entities.fact: Pulley Ridge, off south-west Florida, is a drowned reef holding some of the deepest light-dependent coral in US waters.

entities.name: Galaxy coral
entities.fact: Galaxy coral stings its neighbours with long sweeper tentacles that extend at night.

entities.name: Flowerpot coral
entities.fact: Flowerpot coral has flower-like polyps on stalks that sway in the current.

entities.name: Elegance coral
entities.fact: Elegance coral is a large stony coral with a fleshy, wavy-edged body that lives unattached on sandy seabeds.

entities.name: Scroll coral
entities.fact: Scroll corals grow as wavy, curled plates that can resemble cabbage leaves or vases.

entities.name: Xenia
entities.fact: Xenia are soft corals whose feathery polyps pulse open and shut in a rhythmic, hand-clasping motion.

entities.name: Devonshire cup coral
entities.fact: The Devonshire cup coral is a solitary, cup-shaped stony coral found around British and Irish coasts.

entities.name: Angel skin coral
entities.fact: Angel skin coral is a pale pink precious coral harvested for jewellery and related to red coral.

entities.name: Wire coral
entities.fact: Wire corals are black corals that grow as a single, unbranched, wire-like whip or spiral.

entities.name: Rose coral
entities.fact: The rose coral is an Atlantic stony coral that lives loose on sand and seagrass rather than fixed to rock.

entities.name: Smooth flower coral
entities.fact: The smooth flower coral forms bushy colonies of large, fleshy flower-like polyps on Caribbean reefs.

entities.name: Ivory tree coral
entities.fact: Ivory tree coral forms fragile branching thickets in deep water off Florida and is protected in the Oculina Banks reserve.

entities.name: Red tree coral
entities.fact: Red tree coral forms branching colonies in cold deep water of the North Atlantic and can live for centuries.

entities.name: Pink sea fan
entities.fact: The pink sea fan is a branching gorgonian of British and Mediterranean waters, protected by law in the UK.

entities.name: Bird's nest coral
entities.fact: Bird's nest coral grows as thin, tightly branching colonies with pointed tips that resemble a tangled nest.

entities.name: Open brain coral
entities.fact: The open brain coral is a large, fleshy single-polyp stony coral that lives unattached on sandy seabeds.

entities.name: Honeycomb coral
entities.fact: Honeycomb corals form rounded colonies whose polyps share thin walls, giving a honeycomb pattern.

entities.name: Golden trevally
entities.fact: Young golden trevally swim beside sharks and other large animals like pilot fish, looking like a striped escort.

entities.name: Coral guard crab
entities.fact: Coral guard crabs live among the branches of a coral and defend it against predators such as crown-of-thorns starfish.

entities.name: Xenobalanus
entities.fact: Xenobalanus is a long-stalked barnacle that attaches to the fins and flukes of dolphins and whales.

entities.name: Tubicinella major
entities.fact: Tubicinella major is a barnacle that burrows into the skin of southern right whales, leaving only its top exposed.

entities.name: Pennella
entities.fact: Pennella is a parasitic copepod that buries its head in the flesh of whales and fish, trailing a long egg-bearing body.

entities.name: Prideaux's hermit crab
entities.fact: Prideaux's hermit crab carries a cloak anemone on its shell, gaining protection while the anemone gets scraps and a ride.

entities.name: Cloak anemone
entities.fact: The cloak anemone wraps around a hermit crab's shell and extends it as the crab grows, saving the crab from having to move house.

entities.name: Parasitic anemone
entities.fact: The parasitic anemone rides on hermit crab shells, and in return stings the crab's enemies.

entities.name: Hydractinia
entities.fact: Hydractinia is a colonial hydroid that coats hermit crab shells in a fuzzy fur and helps defend the crab.

entities.name: Urchin clingfish
entities.fact: The urchin clingfish shelters among the long spines of sea urchins and hides there by day.

entities.name: Crinoid clingfish
entities.fact: The crinoid clingfish lives on feather stars and blends in with the colours of its host.

entities.name: Roving coralgrouper
entities.fact: The roving coralgrouper hunts in partnership with giant morays, signalling to them with headstands and head shakes.

entities.name: Venus flower basket shrimp
entities.fact: A pair of these shrimp lives inside a Venus flower basket sponge, growing too big to leave and spending their lives there together.

entities.name: Romanche Trench
entities.fact: The Romanche Trench is a deep fracture-zone trench in the equatorial Atlantic that cuts through the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

entities.name: Cotabato Trench
entities.fact: The Cotabato Trench lies off Mindanao in the Philippines and was the source of the 1976 Moro Gulf earthquake and tsunami.

entities.name: Timor Trough
entities.fact: The Timor Trough is a deep seabed trench lying between the island of Timor and northern Australia.

entities.name: Macquarie Trench
entities.fact: The Macquarie Trench lies south of New Zealand along the Macquarie Ridge, where two tectonic plates meet.

entities.name: Pliny Trench
entities.fact: The Pliny Trench is one of the deep trenches of the Hellenic subduction zone south of Crete in the eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: Strabo Trench
entities.fact: The Strabo Trench is one of the deep trenches of the Hellenic subduction zone south of Crete in the eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: Muertos Trough
entities.fact: The Muertos Trough is a seabed trench in the Caribbean, south of Puerto Rico and Hispaniola.

entities.name: Guatemala Trench
entities.fact: The Guatemala Trench is the section of the Middle America Trench off the Pacific coast of Guatemala.

entities.name: Acapulco Trench
entities.fact: The Acapulco Trench is the section of the Middle America Trench off the Pacific coast of Mexico near Acapulco.

entities.name: Sagami Trough
entities.fact: The Sagami Trough lies off the Pacific coast of Japan near Tokyo Bay, and is linked with the great Kanto earthquake of 1923.

entities.name: Suruga Trough
entities.fact: The Suruga Trough off the coast of Shizuoka in Japan forms the north-eastern end of the Nankai Trough.

entities.name: Diamantina Trench
entities.fact: The Diamantina Trench is a deep trench-like feature in the Indian Ocean south-west of Australia.

entities.name: Kattegat
entities.fact: The Kattegat is the sea between Denmark and Sweden that connects the Baltic Sea to the North Sea through the Skagerrak.

entities.name: Norwegian Sea
entities.fact: The Norwegian Sea lies between Norway and Iceland, and warm Atlantic water flowing through it keeps Norway's coast ice-free.

entities.name: German Bight
entities.fact: The German Bight is the south-eastern bay of the North Sea, into which the Elbe and Weser rivers flow.

entities.name: Cape Cod Bay
entities.fact: Cape Cod Bay is the bay enclosed by the hook of Cape Cod in Massachusetts and a feeding ground for North Atlantic right whales.

entities.name: Massachusetts Bay
entities.fact: Massachusetts Bay is the broad bay on the Gulf of Maine that holds Boston Harbor and, at its mouth, Stellwagen Bank.

entities.name: Tampa Bay
entities.fact: Tampa Bay is Florida's largest open-water estuary, on the Gulf of Mexico.

entities.name: Biscayne Bay
entities.fact: Biscayne Bay is a shallow lagoon beside Miami in Florida, and much of it is protected as a national park.

entities.name: Table Bay
entities.fact: Table Bay is the Atlantic bay beneath Table Mountain at Cape Town, with Robben Island at its mouth.

entities.name: Gulf of Maracaibo
entities.fact: The Gulf of Maracaibo is a Caribbean inlet of Venezuela that connects with Lake Maracaibo, and the region is rich in oil.

entities.name: Golfo Nuevo
entities.fact: Golfo Nuevo is a sheltered gulf on Argentina's Valdes Peninsula where southern right whales gather to breed.

entities.name: Galway Bay
entities.fact: Galway Bay is a large Atlantic bay on the west coast of Ireland, backed by the Burren and the city of Galway.

entities.name: Bantry Bay
entities.fact: Bantry Bay is a long, deep inlet on Ireland's south-west coast, where a French invasion fleet failed to land in 1796.

entities.name: Mobile Bay
entities.fact: Mobile Bay is the Alabama inlet of the Gulf of Mexico, where a famous naval battle was fought in 1864.

entities.name: Java Sea
entities.fact: The Java Sea is a shallow sea between Java and Borneo, where a major naval battle was fought in 1942.

entities.name: Arafura Sea
entities.fact: The Arafura Sea is a shallow sea between northern Australia and New Guinea.

entities.name: Visayan Sea
entities.fact: The Visayan Sea lies in the central Philippines and is an important fishing ground.

entities.name: Manila Bay
entities.fact: Manila Bay is a large natural harbour on the Philippine island of Luzon, known for its sunsets and the 1898 battle fought there.

entities.name: Prince William Sound
entities.fact: Prince William Sound in Alaska was the scene of the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.

entities.name: Hauraki Gulf
entities.fact: The Hauraki Gulf is the island-studded gulf beside Auckland in New Zealand, and home to Bryde's whales.

entities.name: Moreton Bay
entities.fact: Moreton Bay lies off Brisbane in Australia and is a marine park with dugongs, turtles and great sand islands.

entities.name: Suruga Bay
entities.fact: Suruga Bay is the deepest bay in Japan and is known for the Japanese spider crab.

entities.name: Sagami Bay
entities.fact: Sagami Bay is a deep Japanese bay south of Tokyo, where deep-sea animals can be found close to shore.

entities.name: Gulf of Nicoya
entities.fact: The Gulf of Nicoya is a large gulf on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica, fringed with mangroves.

entities.name: Gulf of Guayaquil
entities.fact: The Gulf of Guayaquil is a large gulf on the Pacific coast of South America, shared by Ecuador and Peru.

entities.name: Hawke Bay
entities.fact: Hawke Bay is a wide bay on the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, with Napier on its shore.

entities.name: San Diego Bay
entities.fact: San Diego Bay is a sheltered natural harbour in southern California and home to a major naval base.

entities.name: Ise Bay
entities.fact: Ise Bay is a large bay on the Pacific coast of Japan, with the port of Nagoya at its head.

entities.name: La Pérouse Strait
entities.fact: The La Pérouse Strait separates Hokkaido from the Russian island of Sakhalin, linking the Sea of Japan and the Sea of Okhotsk.

entities.name: Foveaux Strait
entities.fact: Foveaux Strait separates New Zealand's South Island from Stewart Island and is famous for its oysters.

entities.name: Menai Strait
entities.fact: The Menai Strait separates the island of Anglesey from mainland Wales and is crossed by Telford's suspension bridge.

entities.name: Solent
entities.fact: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, famed for yachting and its unusual double high tides.

entities.name: Strait of Belle Isle
entities.fact: The Strait of Belle Isle separates Newfoundland from Labrador and links the Gulf of St Lawrence with the open Atlantic.

entities.name: Strait of Sicily
entities.fact: The Strait of Sicily lies between Sicily and Tunisia and divides the Mediterranean into its eastern and western basins.

entities.name: Fram Strait
entities.fact: The Fram Strait between Greenland and Svalbard is the main gateway for water and sea ice between the Arctic Ocean and the Atlantic.

entities.name: Mozambique Current
entities.fact: The Mozambique Current flows south through the Mozambique Channel in a chain of large eddies and helps feed the Agulhas Current.

entities.name: East Madagascar Current
entities.fact: The East Madagascar Current flows south along the east coast of Madagascar and is one of the sources of the Agulhas Current.

entities.name: Azores Current
entities.fact: The Azores Current is an eastward branch of the Gulf Stream system that crosses the Atlantic near the Azores.

entities.name: Portugal Current
entities.fact: The Portugal Current is a slow, cool current flowing south off Portugal as part of the North Atlantic gyre and feeding the Canary Current.

entities.name: Caribbean Current
entities.fact: The Caribbean Current carries warm water west through the Caribbean Sea towards the Yucatan Channel and the Loop Current.

entities.name: Guiana Current
entities.fact: The Guiana Current flows north-west along the north-east coast of South America, carrying Amazon water and sediment.

entities.name: North Brazil Current
entities.fact: The North Brazil Current flows north-west along the coast of Brazil and sheds huge rings of water that drift into the Caribbean.

entities.name: Tsushima Current
entities.fact: The Tsushima Current is a warm branch of the Kuroshio that flows through the Korea Strait into the Sea of Japan.

entities.name: Mindanao Current
entities.fact: The Mindanao Current flows south along the east coast of the Philippines, carrying warm Pacific water towards Indonesia.

entities.name: North Pacific Current
entities.fact: The North Pacific Current is the broad eastward continuation of the Kuroshio across the North Pacific.

entities.name: Kamchatka Current
entities.fact: The Kamchatka Current is a cold current flowing south-west along the Kamchatka coast that feeds the Oyashio.

entities.name: Agulhas Return Current
entities.fact: The Agulhas Return Current is the eastward flow formed when the Agulhas Current turns back on itself south of Africa.

entities.name: Southland Current
entities.fact: The Southland Current carries subtropical water north-east along the southern and eastern coast of New Zealand's South Island.

entities.name: Cape Horn Current
entities.fact: The Cape Horn Current is a cold current flowing east around the southern tip of South America.

entities.name: West Greenland Current
entities.fact: The West Greenland Current carries water north along Greenland's west coast towards Baffin Bay.

entities.name: Angola Current
entities.fact: The Angola Current is a warm current flowing south along the coast of Angola until it meets the cold Benguela Current.

entities.name: Weddell Gyre
entities.fact: The Weddell Gyre is a huge clockwise circulation in the Southern Ocean off Antarctica, where cold dense bottom water forms.

entities.name: Ross Gyre
entities.fact: The Ross Gyre is a large clockwise circulation in the Southern Ocean beside Antarctica's Ross Sea.

entities.name: Indonesian Throughflow
entities.fact: The Indonesian Throughflow carries warm water from the Pacific into the Indian Ocean through the seas of Indonesia.

entities.name: Moorea
entities.fact: Moorea is a heart-shaped volcanic island in French Polynesia, a short ferry ride from Tahiti.

entities.name: Oahu
entities.fact: Oahu is the Hawaiian island that holds Honolulu, Pearl Harbor and Waikiki.

entities.name: Maui
entities.fact: Maui is the Hawaiian island whose waters host breeding humpback whales each winter.

entities.name: Kauai
entities.fact: Kauai is the oldest of the main Hawaiian islands and has one of the wettest spots on Earth, Mount Waialeale.

entities.name: Pohnpei
entities.fact: Pohnpei is a high volcanic island in Micronesia, home to Nan Madol, a city built on coral reef islets.

entities.name: Chuuk
entities.fact: Chuuk, once called Truk, is a Micronesian island group whose lagoon holds dozens of Second World War shipwrecks.

entities.name: Saipan
entities.fact: Saipan is the largest island of the Northern Mariana Islands and the site of a major battle in 1944.

entities.name: Norfolk Island
entities.fact: Norfolk Island is a small Australian territory in the south-west Pacific, once a penal colony and famous for its tall Norfolk pines.

entities.name: Stewart Island
entities.fact: Stewart Island, called Rakiura in Maori, is New Zealand's third-largest island and a refuge for kiwi.

entities.name: Macquarie Island
entities.fact: Macquarie Island is a remote sub-Antarctic island between Tasmania and Antarctica, breeding ground for king penguins and elephant seals.

entities.name: Haida Gwaii
entities.fact: Haida Gwaii is an archipelago off the coast of British Columbia, the homeland of the Haida people.

entities.name: Chiloe
entities.fact: Chiloe is a large island off southern Chile, known for its wooden churches and houses built on stilts.

entities.name: Wake Island
entities.fact: Wake Island is a remote coral atoll in the north Pacific and the site of a fierce battle in 1941.

entities.name: Nantucket
entities.fact: Nantucket is a small island off Cape Cod that was one of the leading whaling ports of the 1800s.

entities.name: Martha's Vineyard
entities.fact: Martha's Vineyard is a Massachusetts island south of Cape Cod and a popular summer retreat.

entities.name: Cape Breton Island
entities.fact: Cape Breton Island forms the northern part of Nova Scotia and is known for the scenic Cabot Trail.

entities.name: Prince Edward Island
entities.fact: Prince Edward Island is Canada's smallest province, a red-soiled island in the Gulf of St Lawrence.

entities.name: Isle of Man
entities.fact: The Isle of Man sits in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland and is famous for its Tourist Trophy motorcycle races.

entities.name: Isle of Wight
entities.fact: The Isle of Wight lies off the south coast of England beside the Solent and is rich in dinosaur fossils.

entities.name: Lundy
entities.fact: Lundy is a granite island in the Bristol Channel and the site of Britain's first marine nature reserve.

entities.name: St Kilda
entities.fact: St Kilda is a remote Scottish archipelago with huge seabird colonies, abandoned by its people in 1930.

entities.name: Gough Island
entities.fact: Gough Island is a remote South Atlantic island and nature reserve, home to enormous seabird colonies.

entities.name: Heligoland
entities.fact: Heligoland is a small red-sandstone German island in the North Sea.

entities.name: Texel
entities.fact: Texel is the largest of the Dutch Wadden Sea islands.

entities.name: Lofoten
entities.fact: The Lofoten islands lie off northern Norway and are known for steep peaks and winter cod fishing.

entities.name: Lazarev Sea
entities.fact: The Lazarev Sea off Antarctica is named after the Russian admiral Mikhail Lazarev, who sailed on Bellingshausen's Antarctic voyage.

entities.name: Riiser-Larsen Sea
entities.fact: The Riiser-Larsen Sea off Antarctica is named after the Norwegian aviator and explorer Hjalmar Riiser-Larsen.

entities.name: Davis Sea
entities.fact: The Davis Sea off Antarctica is named after Captain John King Davis, who commanded Mawson's expedition ship Aurora.

entities.name: Mawson Sea
entities.fact: The Mawson Sea off Antarctica is named after the Australian explorer Douglas Mawson.

entities.name: D'Urville Sea
entities.fact: The D'Urville Sea off Antarctica is named after the French explorer Jules Dumont d'Urville, who sailed along the coast in 1840.

entities.name: Somov Sea
entities.fact: The Somov Sea off Antarctica is named after the Soviet oceanographer Mikhail Somov, who led the first Soviet Antarctic expedition.

entities.name: Prydz Bay
entities.fact: Prydz Bay in East Antarctica is named after the Norwegian whaling captain Olaf Prydz.

entities.name: McMurdo Sound
entities.fact: McMurdo Sound in Antarctica is named after Lieutenant Archibald McMurdo of HMS Terror and lies off the main US research station.

entities.name: Cook Inlet
entities.fact: Cook Inlet in Alaska is named after Captain James Cook, who explored it in 1778.

entities.name: Spencer Gulf
entities.fact: Spencer Gulf in South Australia was named by Matthew Flinders after George Spencer, the Earl Spencer.

entities.name: Le Maire Strait
entities.fact: The Le Maire Strait, between Tierra del Fuego and Isla de los Estados, is named after the Dutch navigator Jacob Le Maire.

entities.name: Scoresby Sound
entities.fact: Scoresby Sound in east Greenland is named after the British whaler and explorer William Scoresby and is one of the largest fjord systems in the world.

entities.name: Bay of Kotor
entities.fact: The Bay of Kotor in Montenegro is a winding, fjord-like inlet of the Adriatic ringed by steep mountains.

entities.name: Ambracian Gulf
entities.fact: The Ambracian Gulf on Greece's west coast lies beside Actium, where Octavian's fleet defeated Mark Antony in 31 BC.

entities.name: Gulf of Patras
entities.fact: The Gulf of Patras in western Greece opens to the Ionian Sea, and the port of Patras sits on its shore.

entities.name: Gulf of Izmir
entities.fact: The Gulf of Izmir is a long inlet of the Aegean on Turkey's coast, with the city of Izmir at its head.

entities.name: Gulf of Gokova
entities.fact: The Gulf of Gokova is a long, sheltered gulf on Turkey's south-west coast, popular for sailing and protected as a marine area.

entities.name: Bay of Haifa
entities.fact: The Bay of Haifa is the Mediterranean bay in northern Israel on which the port of Haifa sits.

entities.name: Gulf of Gaeta
entities.fact: The Gulf of Gaeta is a gulf of the Tyrrhenian Sea in central Italy, with the town of Gaeta on its shore.

entities.name: Gulf of Manfredonia
entities.fact: The Gulf of Manfredonia is a gulf of the Adriatic on the south side of the Gargano peninsula in Italy.

entities.name: Gulf of La Spezia
entities.fact: The Gulf of La Spezia is a deep natural harbour on the Ligurian coast, nicknamed the Gulf of Poets.

entities.name: Gulf of Orosei
entities.fact: The Gulf of Orosei on the east coast of Sardinia is lined with limestone cliffs and hidden coves.

entities.name: Gulf of Palermo
entities.fact: The Gulf of Palermo is the bay on Sicily's north coast in which the island's capital sits.

entities.name: Gulf of Valencia
entities.fact: The Gulf of Valencia is a broad gulf on Spain's east coast, with the city of Valencia on its shore.

entities.name: Sea of Corsica
entities.fact: The Sea of Corsica lies between the island of Corsica and the Tuscan Archipelago.

entities.name: Sea Cliff
entities.fact: Sea Cliff was a US Navy deep-submergence submersible rated to roughly 6,000 metres.

entities.name: Jason
entities.fact: Jason is a remotely operated vehicle of Woods Hole that explores hydrothermal vents and wrecks from a ship at the surface.

entities.name: Sentry
entities.fact: Sentry is an autonomous underwater vehicle from Woods Hole that surveys the deep seafloor without a cable to the ship.

entities.name: Pisces V
entities.fact: Pisces V is a research submersible operated from Hawaii that has explored undersea volcanoes such as Loihi.

entities.name: Shinkai 2000
entities.fact: Shinkai 2000 was a Japanese crewed research submersible that could dive to 2,000 metres.

entities.name: FNRS-2
entities.fact: FNRS-2 was the first bathyscaphe, designed by Auguste Piccard and tested off Cape Verde in 1948.

entities.name: RRS James Clark Ross
entities.fact: RRS James Clark Ross is a British polar research ship, launched in 1990 and named after the Antarctic explorer.

entities.name: RRS Charles Darwin
entities.fact: RRS Charles Darwin was a British ocean research ship, launched in 1984, used to study the deep sea.

entities.name: Belgica
entities.fact: The Belgica carried the Belgian Antarctic Expedition of 1897 to 1899, the first to spend a winter trapped in Antarctic pack ice.

entities.name: Vityaz
entities.fact: The Soviet research ship Vityaz took deep soundings of the Mariana Trench in 1957 and found a depth of around 11,000 metres.

entities.name: Valdivia
entities.fact: The German steamship Valdivia carried the 1898 to 1899 Deep Sea Expedition, which collected animals from the deep ocean.

entities.name: Carnegie
entities.fact: The Carnegie was a wooden, non-magnetic research yacht that surveyed the oceans until it exploded in 1929.

entities.name: Atlantis II
entities.fact: Atlantis II was a Woods Hole research ship that served as Alvin's mother ship for decades.

entities.name: Pourquoi-Pas?
entities.fact: Pourquoi-Pas? was Jean-Baptiste Charcot's polar research ship, which sank off Iceland in 1936.

entities.name: Cyana
entities.fact: Cyana was a French research submersible that joined the 1974 FAMOUS expedition to the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

entities.name: Henry Hudson
entities.fact: Henry Hudson explored the river, strait and bay that now bear his name while seeking a northern route to Asia, and was cast adrift by his crew in 1611.

entities.name: Vitus Bering
entities.fact: Vitus Bering was a Danish-born Russian navigator who sailed through the strait now named after him in 1728.

entities.name: Abel Tasman
entities.fact: Abel Tasman was a Dutch navigator who in 1642 became the first European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand.

entities.name: Jacques Cartier
entities.fact: Jacques Cartier was a French navigator who explored the Gulf of St Lawrence and sailed up the great river in the 1530s.

entities.name: George Vancouver
entities.fact: George Vancouver was a Royal Navy officer who surveyed the Pacific north-west coast of North America between 1791 and 1795.

entities.name: Joshua Slocum
entities.fact: Joshua Slocum was the first person to sail alone around the world, finishing the voyage in 1898 in the sloop Spray.

entities.name: Edith Widder
entities.fact: Edith Widder is a deep-sea biologist who led the team that filmed a live giant squid in its natural habitat in 2012, using a glowing lure.

entities.name: Valerie Taylor
entities.fact: Valerie Taylor is an Australian diver, filmmaker and shark conservationist whose shark footage featured in the film Jaws.

entities.name: David Doubilet
entities.fact: David Doubilet is an American underwater photographer who has photographed the sea for National Geographic for decades.

entities.name: Rodney Fox
entities.fact: Rodney Fox survived a great white shark attack in 1963 and went on to pioneer shark cage diving.

entities.name: Harold Edgerton
entities.fact: Harold Edgerton was an American engineer who perfected the electronic flash and worked with Jacques Cousteau on underwater photography and sonar.

entities.name: Maurice Ewing
entities.fact: Maurice Ewing founded the Lamont Geological Observatory and led research into the structure of the ocean floor.

entities.name: Edwin Link
entities.fact: Edwin Link, the inventor of the flight simulator, designed submersibles and pioneered living underwater for days at a time.

entities.name: John Murray
entities.fact: John Murray was a Scottish-Canadian oceanographer who served on the Challenger expedition and edited its reports.

entities.name: Kathryn Sullivan
entities.fact: Kathryn Sullivan was the first American woman to walk in space, and in 2020 became the first woman to reach Challenger Deep.

entities.name: Cindy Van Dover
entities.fact: Cindy Van Dover was the first woman to pilot the submersible Alvin, and she studies life at hydrothermal vents.

entities.name: Enzo Maiorca
entities.fact: Enzo Maiorca was an Italian freediver who in 1961 became the first person to dive below 50 metres on a single breath.

entities.name: William Trubridge
entities.fact: William Trubridge is a New Zealand freediver who has set world records diving without fins or any pull on a rope.

entities.name: Tanya Streeter
entities.fact: Tanya Streeter, a freediver from the Cayman Islands, set a no-limits world record of 160 metres in 2002.

entities.name: Enric Sala
entities.fact: Enric Sala is a Spanish marine ecologist who founded National Geographic's Pristine Seas project to protect wild parts of the ocean.

entities.name: Edmund Fitzgerald
entities.fact: The Great Lakes freighter Edmund Fitzgerald sank in a Lake Superior storm in 1975 with all 29 crew, and was immortalised in a Gordon Lightfoot song.

entities.name: Scharnhorst
entities.fact: The German battleship Scharnhorst was sunk off North Cape, Norway, in December 1943 after a battle with British warships.

entities.name: Tirpitz
entities.fact: The German battleship Tirpitz was sunk by RAF bombers near Tromso, Norway, in November 1944.

entities.name: HMS Prince of Wales
entities.fact: The battleship HMS Prince of Wales was sunk by Japanese aircraft off Malaya in December 1941, days after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

entities.name: USS Juneau
entities.fact: The US cruiser USS Juneau was sunk off Guadalcanal in 1942, and all five Sullivan brothers aboard were lost.

entities.name: Savannah
entities.fact: Savannah is a historic Georgia port city, home to one of the busiest container ports on the US east coast.

entities.name: Jacksonville
entities.fact: Jacksonville in Florida sits on the St Johns River close to the Atlantic and has a major deepwater port and naval base.

entities.name: Recife
entities.fact: Recife is a Brazilian Atlantic port city of rivers and bridges, built partly on islands.

entities.name: Fortaleza
entities.fact: Fortaleza is a Brazilian port city on the Atlantic coast of the north-east.

entities.name: Tangier
entities.fact: Tangier is a Moroccan port at the western entrance of the Strait of Gibraltar, where the Mediterranean meets the Atlantic.

entities.name: Agadir
entities.fact: Agadir is a Moroccan port city on the Atlantic coast, rebuilt after the great earthquake of 1960.

entities.name: La Rochelle
entities.fact: La Rochelle is a French Atlantic port whose old harbour is guarded by medieval towers.

entities.name: Galway
entities.fact: Galway is a port city on Ireland's west coast, at the mouth of the River Corrib on Galway Bay.

entities.name: Bergen
entities.fact: Bergen is a Norwegian port on the North Sea coast, with the old Hanseatic wharf of Bryggen.

entities.name: Tromso
entities.fact: Tromso is a Norwegian port city north of the Arctic Circle and a base for polar expeditions.

entities.name: Monrovia
entities.fact: Monrovia is the capital and main port of Liberia, on the Atlantic coast of West Africa.

entities.name: Banjul
entities.fact: Banjul is the capital of The Gambia, on an island where the Gambia River meets the Atlantic.

entities.name: Setubal
entities.fact: Setubal is a Portuguese port on the Sado estuary, known for its resident bottlenose dolphins.

entities.name: Brigantine
entities.fact: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship with a square-rigged foremast and a fore-and-aft rigged mainmast.

entities.name: Brig
entities.fact: A brig is a two-masted sailing ship with square sails on both masts.

entities.name: Barque
entities.fact: A barque is a sailing ship of three or more masts, square-rigged on all but the last mast.

entities.name: Ketch
entities.fact: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat whose shorter mizzen mast stands forward of the rudder post.

entities.name: Yawl
entities.fact: A yawl is a two-masted sailboat whose small mizzen mast is stepped behind the rudder post.

entities.name: Lugger
entities.fact: A lugger is a small sailing vessel rigged with lugsails, once widely used for fishing and smuggling around Britain.

entities.name: Fluyt
entities.fact: The fluyt was a Dutch cargo ship of the 1600s, designed to carry large loads with a small crew.

entities.name: Caique
entities.fact: A caique is a traditional wooden fishing boat of the Aegean and eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: Proa
entities.fact: The proa is a Pacific sailing canoe with an outrigger float, famed for its speed.

entities.name: Trimaran
entities.fact: A trimaran is a boat with a central hull and two smaller hulls on either side.

entities.name: Icebreaker
entities.fact: An icebreaker is a ship with a strengthened hull that smashes a channel through sea ice.

entities.name: Paddle steamer
entities.fact: A paddle steamer is driven by a steam engine turning paddle wheels at its sides or stern.

entities.name: Drifter
entities.fact: A drifter is a fishing boat that lets its nets drift with the current, and was once the mainstay of the herring fleets.

entities.name: Gracilaria
entities.fact: Gracilaria is a red seaweed farmed widely around the world as a source of agar.

entities.name: Arame
entities.fact: Arame is a brown kelp harvested in Japan and eaten shredded after soaking and boiling.

entities.name: Sea oak
entities.fact: The sea oak is a brown seaweed of rock pools and shallow seas whose branches carry pod-like air bladders.

entities.name: Japanese wireweed
entities.fact: Japanese wireweed is a fast-growing brown seaweed from the Pacific that has invaded the coasts of Europe and North America.

entities.name: Mermaid's wineglass
entities.fact: Mermaid's wineglass is a single-celled green alga shaped like a tiny goblet that grows several centimetres tall.

entities.name: Forest kelp
entities.fact: Forest kelp forms dense underwater forests around north-west Europe, with tough stalks that can live for many years.

entities.name: Furbelows
entities.fact: Furbelows is a brown seaweed with a warty bulb-like holdfast and a frilly ribbon-like frond that is often washed ashore in summer.

entities.name: Mozuku
entities.fact: Mozuku is a slimy brown seaweed farmed in Okinawa and eaten with vinegar.

entities.name: North Ronaldsay sheep
entities.fact: North Ronaldsay sheep live almost entirely on seaweed, kept off the grass of their Orkney island by a long stone wall.

entities.name: Kelp goose
entities.fact: The kelp goose of southern South America feeds on seaweed along rocky shores, and the male is white while the female is dark.

entities.name: Black swan
entities.fact: Black swans graze on algae and water plants, including seagrass in estuaries, and are native to Australia.

entities.name: Luderick
entities.fact: The luderick is a common Australian estuary fish that grazes mostly on green algae.

entities.name: Emerald crab
entities.fact: Emerald crabs graze algae on Caribbean reefs and are kept in aquariums to keep algae in check.

entities.name: Ark shell
entities.fact: The ark shell, called akagai in Japan, is a red-fleshed clam served as sushi, its colour coming from haemoglobin in its blood.

entities.name: Splendid alfonsino
entities.fact: The splendid alfonsino, kinmedai in Japan, is a red deep-water fish with large golden eyes, served as sushi and sashimi.

entities.name: Blackthroat seaperch
entities.fact: The blackthroat seaperch, nodoguro in Japan, is a fatty deep-water fish prized for sushi and grilling, named for its black mouth lining.

entities.name: Australian bonito
entities.fact: The Australian bonito is a small tuna-like fish of southern Australian and New Zealand waters, sought by anglers.

entities.name: Black skipjack
entities.fact: The black skipjack is a small tuna of the eastern Pacific, marked with dark stripes along its belly.

entities.name: Monterey Spanish mackerel
entities.fact: The Monterey Spanish mackerel is named after Monterey Bay in California, where it was once abundant.

entities.name: Serra Spanish mackerel
entities.fact: The serra Spanish mackerel is a fast-swimming mackerel of the western Atlantic, from the Caribbean down to Brazil.

entities.name: Broad-barred Spanish mackerel
entities.fact: The broad-barred Spanish mackerel is a fast mackerel of northern Australian and New Guinea waters, named for its wide dark bars.

entities.name: Korean mackerel
entities.fact: The Korean mackerel is a Spanish mackerel found from the Indian Ocean to the seas around Korea and China.

entities.name: Streaked seerfish
entities.fact: The streaked seerfish is an Indo-Pacific mackerel marked with streaks of dark spots along its sides.

entities.name: Indo-Pacific king mackerel
entities.fact: The Indo-Pacific king mackerel is a large, fast mackerel of the Indian Ocean and western Pacific and an important food fish.

entities.name: Atlantic chub mackerel
entities.fact: The Atlantic chub mackerel forms big schools in the Atlantic and Mediterranean and is caught for food.

entities.name: Short mackerel
entities.fact: The short mackerel is a plankton-feeding mackerel of the Indo-West Pacific, heavily fished and eaten in Thailand.

entities.name: Australian spotted mackerel
entities.fact: The Australian spotted mackerel is a fast mackerel of northern Australian waters, valued by anglers and commercial fishers.

entities.name: Leaping bonito
entities.fact: The leaping bonito is a small tuna relative of northern Australian waters.

entities.name: Pacific tomcod
entities.fact: The Pacific tomcod is a small cod of North America's Pacific coast, closely related to the Atlantic tomcod.

entities.name: Saffron cod
entities.fact: The saffron cod is a small cod of the North Pacific and Arctic seas, fished by coastal communities in Alaska and Russia.

entities.name: Fivebeard rockling
entities.fact: The fivebeard rockling is a small cod relative with five barbels around its mouth, found in rock pools and shallow water around Europe.

entities.name: Fourbeard rockling
entities.fact: The fourbeard rockling is a small cod relative of the North Atlantic with four barbels near its mouth.

entities.name: Threebeard rockling
entities.fact: The threebeard rockling is a cod relative of north-east Atlantic coastal waters with three barbels on its head.

entities.name: Blue ling
entities.fact: The blue ling is a deep-water relative of the cod in the north-east Atlantic that can grow longer than a metre.

entities.name: Spanish ling
entities.fact: The Spanish ling is a deep-water relative of the ling found in the north-east Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

entities.name: Red hake
entities.fact: The red hake is a western Atlantic hake with long, thread-like pelvic fins that it uses to feel along the seabed.

entities.name: Spotted hake
entities.fact: The spotted hake is a small western Atlantic hake marked with a dark spot on its first dorsal fin.

entities.name: Chilean hake
entities.fact: The Chilean hake is a major commercial fish of the Pacific coasts of Chile and Peru.

entities.name: Pacific hake
entities.fact: The Pacific hake, also called Pacific whiting, is caught in huge numbers off the Pacific coast of North America.

entities.name: Deepwater Cape hake
entities.fact: The deepwater Cape hake lives in deeper water off southern Africa and is a major catch of South African and Namibian trawlers.

entities.name: Tadpole fish
entities.fact: The tadpole fish is a small, big-headed relative of the cod found on rocky coasts of the north-east Atlantic.
